  ✗ [CC-001] Clarity & Communication: Response is hard to follow and contains misleading information about question formation. (flagged 2 times)

critic_scores.rationale: The response still contains critical factual errors that were flagged in previous rounds. It incorrectly implies that 'nej' (no) is central to forming yes/no questions in Swedish, when in fact Swedish yes/no questions (ja/nej-frågor) are formed by inverting the subject and verb — placing the verb first in the sentence. The core rule (verb-subject inversion) is entirely absent, and the claim about 'nej' remains misleading and unresolved from FC-001.
critic_scores.improvement_tip: Clearly state the actual rule: in Swedish, yes/no questions are formed by placing the verb before the subject (subject-verb inversion), e.g., 'Du talar svenska.' (You speak Swedish.) becomes 'Talar du svenska?' (Do you speak Swedish?). Remove all references to 'nej' as a structural element of question formation.

critic_scores.rationale: The response remains confusing and incoherent, failing to correct the fundamental factual error regarding the formation of yes/no questions in Swedish. The structure is still unclear, and the explanation does not provide a comprehensive understanding of the topic.
